What is ragi?

Ragi (also known as Finger Millet or Nachni) is a highly nutritious ancient grain renowned as the calcium powerhouse among cereals, containing around 344mg of calcium per 100g. It is commonly used in foods such as porridge, malt, dosa, roti, and baked products. MilletVerse provides educational insights, recipes, and clean-label marketplace products to help users easily integrate Ragi into their daily diets.

What are millets and why are they called nutri-cereals?

Millets are a family of small-seeded annual grasses cultivated for thousands of years as staple food grains. They are called 'Nutri-Cereals' because they pack an exceptional concentration of dietary fiber, plant protein, essential minerals (like calcium and iron), and antioxidants compared to refined grains. Additionally, millets are drought-tolerant and climate-resilient, requiring minimal water and chemical inputs to grow.

What are the different types of millets available?

Major millets include Ragi (Finger Millet - calcium rich), Jowar (Sorghum - heart healthy), and Bajra (Pearl Millet - iron rich). Minor millets include Foxtail Millet (low glycemic index), Barnyard Millet (lowest calories, high fiber), Little Millet (rich in B-vitamins), Kodo Millet (high fiber and lecithin), and Proso Millet (high protein). Each offers distinct culinary and nutritional benefits.

You can seamlessly include millets in your daily routine:
• Breakfast: Enjoy warm Ragi malt, Foxtail millet idlis, or Barnyard millet upma.
• Lunch: Replace refined rotis with Jowar or Bajra bhakri, or swap white rice for steamed Foxtail or Little millet.
• Snacks: Munch on baked Ragi biscuits or roasted Bajra jeera crackers.
• Dinner: Opt for light, easily digestible Bajra-moong khichdi or warm millet soup.

How do I make Ragi chocolate chip cookies at home?

To make Ragi Chocolate Chip Cookies:
• Ingredients: 1 cup Ragi flour, 1/2 cup organic jaggery powder, 1/4 cup melted ghee or coconut oil, 2 tbsp cocoa powder, 1/4 tsp baking soda, 1/4 cup dark chocolate chips, and 2-3 tbsp warm milk.
• Method: Whisk the dry ingredients together. In another bowl, mix melted ghee and jaggery until smooth. Combine both mixtures, adding warm milk to form a soft dough, and gently fold in chocolate chips. Shape into small discs on a lined baking tray.
• Bake: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F) and bake for 12 to 15 minutes. Cool completely on a wire rack to crisp up.

How do I prepare traditional Ragi malt in 5 minutes?

To prepare warm Ragi malt:
1. Whisk 2 tablespoons of Ragi flour into 1/2 cup room-temperature water until lump-free.
2. Cook on medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring continuously until glossy and thick.
3. Pour in 1 cup of warm milk (or water) and simmer for 1-2 minutes.
4. Stir in 1-2 teaspoons of jaggery and a pinch of cardamom powder. Serve warm!

How can a farmer list raw millets on MilletVerse?

Farmers can list raw millets in four straightforward steps:
1. Register on MilletVerse choosing the 'Farmer / Agricultural Producer' role.
2. Submit listing details: grain variety (e.g., Ragi, Bajra, Foxtail), grain form (unhulled/hulled), available quantity in kg or quintals, minimum order size, harvest season, and asking price.
3. Complete quick grain quality and moisture verification (<12% moisture standard).
4. Once verified, the listing is published on our B2B/B2C sourcing exchange for buyers to purchase.
